title: Bringing back the dark
instructions: Read the article about light pollution. Choose the most suitable heading (A–I) for each paragraph (1–6). There are two extra headings that you do not need to use. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Olvasd el a fényszennyezésről szóló cikket, és válaszd ki minden bekezdéshez a legmegfelelőbb címet (A–I). Két cím felesleges. A 0. a példa.

passage.title: Bringing back the dark
passage.subtitle: Light pollution is spreading fast – but it may be the easiest environmental problem to solve

blocks.text: On a clear night in the village of Kellan, high on the moors of northern England, visitors often fall silent when they step out of the pub. Above them, the Milky Way stretches from one horizon to the other like a band of pale smoke. For the people who live here, it is nothing special, but many guests admit that they have never seen it before. That is hardly surprising: according to recent estimates, around six out of ten Europeans live in places where the night sky is so bright that our own galaxy has become invisible.

Measuring how fast the problem is growing has proved surprisingly difficult. Satellites, it turns out, are partly blind to the bluish light of modern street lamps, so scientists turned to ordinary people for help. For more than a decade, tens of thousands of volunteers around the world have gone outside on dark evenings, compared what they could see with a set of star charts and reported the faintest stars visible. When researchers analysed the results, they were alarmed: the sky above the average participant had been getting brighter by almost ten per cent a year. At that rate, a child born today in a place where 250 stars are visible would be able to see fewer than half as many by their eighteenth birthday.

Humans are not the only ones affected. For many animals, darkness is not simply the absence of light but a resource they depend on. Moths and other night-flying insects circle street lamps until they die of exhaustion or are eaten by bats. Baby sea turtles, which instinctively head towards the brightest horizon after hatching, crawl inland towards hotels and roads instead of towards the sea. Migrating birds, which use the stars to navigate, are drawn off course by illuminated towers, and every autumn thousands of them crash into lit-up office blocks.

There is growing evidence that our own bodies suffer too. In darkness, the brain produces melatonin, a hormone that tells the body it is time to rest. Even quite low levels of light – a street lamp shining through thin curtains, for instance – can reduce the amount produced. Studies have linked long-term exposure to artificial light at night with poor sleep, weight gain and even depression, although researchers stress that it is difficult to separate the effect of outdoor lighting from that of the screens most of us stare at before bed.

Ironically, one of the main causes of the recent increase is a technology that was supposed to help the environment. Over the past fifteen years, towns across Europe have replaced their old orange street lamps with LEDs, which use far less electricity. Yet because the new lights are so cheap to run, many councils simply installed more of them, lighting up car parks, sports fields and buildings that had previously been left in darkness. Worse still, the white light of early LEDs contains a high proportion of blue light, which scatters more easily in the atmosphere and therefore spreads further across the sky.

The good news is that, unlike most environmental problems, this one can disappear at the flick of a switch. Lamps can be fitted with shields so that they light only the ground, and warmer, yellower bulbs are available at no extra cost. Some towns have gone further and switch off most of their street lights between one and five in the morning. When the small French town of Saint-Avrel tried this, many residents were convinced that burglaries would increase. Three years later, police figures showed no change at all – and the town's electricity bill had fallen by a third.

For places like Kellan, darkness has even become a source of income. Since the moor was officially recognised as a dark-sky reserve, local guesthouses have been fully booked in the winter months, traditionally the quietest time of the year. A former sheep farmer now leads night-time walks for visitors, and the village school has built a small observatory with money raised by tourists. 'People used to say we lived in the middle of nowhere,' says guesthouse owner Margaret Hallam. 'Now that's exactly why they come.'

options.text: Amateur stargazers reveal a worrying trend
A sight most of us have lost
A green solution with an unexpected side effect
Is artificial light making us ill?

example.explanation: D – A sight most of us have lost. A bekezdés lényege, hogy a Tejút látványa a legtöbb ember számára eltűnt: az európaiak nagyjából hat tizede olyan helyen él, ahol a galaxisunk már nem látható.
example.evidence: around six out of ten Europeans live in places where the night sky is so bright that our own galaxy has become invisible

items.explanation: C – Amateur stargazers reveal a worrying trend. A bekezdés arról szól, hogy önkéntesek (amatőr csillagnézők) megfigyeléseiből derült ki, hogy az égbolt évente közel 10%-kal világosodik – ez a riasztó tendencia („they were alarmed”).
items.evidence: the sky above the average participant had been getting brighter by almost ten per cent a year

wrongOptions.F: Épp az ellenkezője igaz: a műholdak „részben vakok” a modern lámpák kékes fényére, ezért kellett hétköznapi emberek segítségét kérni.

items.explanation: G – Creatures that lose their way. A bekezdés állatokról szól, akiket a mesterséges fény eltérít: a teknősök a tenger helyett a szárazföld felé másznak, a vándormadarakat letérítik útjukról a kivilágított tornyok.
items.evidence: Migrating birds, which use the stars to navigate, are drawn off course by illuminated towers

wrongOptions.I: Az „Is artificial light making us ill?” az emberi egészségről szól (3. bekezdés), ez a bekezdés viszont kifejezetten az állatokról: „Humans are not the only ones affected.”

items.explanation: I – Is artificial light making us ill? A bekezdés a fény emberi egészségre gyakorolt hatásáról szól (melatonin, rossz alvás, hízás, depresszió). A kérdő forma illik ahhoz, hogy a kutatók óvatosak: a hatást nehéz elkülöníteni.
items.evidence: Studies have linked long-term exposure to artificial light at night with poor sleep, weight gain and even depression

wrongOptions.A: A képernyők csak a bekezdés végén kerülnek elő, és a szöveg nem állítja, hogy ők a fő bűnösök – csak annyit, hogy nehéz szétválasztani a két hatást.

items.explanation: E – A green solution with an unexpected side effect. Az energiatakarékos LED-eknek a környezetet kellett volna segíteniük („supposed to help the environment”), de mivel olcsó üzemeltetni őket, többet szereltek fel, és kék fényük messzebbre szóródik – ez a váratlan mellékhatás.
items.evidence: Ironically, one of the main causes of the recent increase is a technology that was supposed to help the environment.

wrongOptions.H: Ebben a bekezdésben nem megoldásról és alaptalan félelmekről van szó, hanem arról, hogyan rontott a helyzeten a LED-technológia.

items.explanation: H – Simple solutions and groundless fears. A bekezdés egyszerű megoldásokat sorol fel (ernyők, melegebb fényű izzók, éjszakai lekapcsolás), és bemutatja, hogy a lakók félelme a betörések növekedésétől alaptalannak bizonyult: a rendőrségi adatok szerint semmi sem változott.
items.evidence: Three years later, police figures showed no change at all

wrongOptions.E: Itt a megoldásoknak nincs váratlan mellékhatásuk – sőt, a villanyszámla is harmadával csökkent.

items.explanation: B – When being remote pays off. A sötétség bevételi forrássá vált: a panziók télen is tele vannak, a turisták pénzéből csillagvizsgáló épült. A „middle of nowhere” (isten háta mögött) jelleg most éppen vonzerő.
items.evidence: 'People used to say we lived in the middle of nowhere,' says guesthouse owner Margaret Hallam. 'Now that's exactly why they come.'

wrongOptions.D: Bár ez a bekezdés is Kellanről szól, a lényege nem az elveszett látvány, hanem az, hogy a sötétség (és az eldugottság) pénzt hoz a falunak.
